Abstract
This research focuses on the design and implementation of an intelligent hybrid model, based on
Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks and Reinforcement Learning (RL), to optimize
API performance in cloud-based microservice architectures. The model analyzes temporal traffic
and workload data to predict resource consumption patterns and, through reinforcement learning
policies, performs dynamic and proactive allocation of computational resources, including CPU,
RAM, and GPU, at the Kubernetes cluster level. Experimental results in a real-world operational
environment demonstrated that the proposed method leads to a 32-38% reduction in average API
response latency, a 30% decrease in SLA violations with an increase in response success rate,
operational cost reductions between 35-50%, a 30-45% decrease in energy consumption, and a 35-
40% increase in scalability. Overall, the combination of reinforcement learning and LSTM
networks in the microservices context proves to be an effective, adaptive, and generalizable
approach for improving Quality of Service (QoS) and intelligent resource management in dynamic,
distributed, and scalable cloud environments.
Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, LSTM Neural Network, Microservices, API, Kubernetes,
Resource Allocation, Quality of Service (QoS), Cloud Computing.
